issues.title: Using assert instead of XCTAssert
issues.description: The rule requires test methods to use assertions from the XCTest framework (XCTAssert family), but standard Swift assert() functions were used instead of XCTAssertTrue()
issues.rule_name: Test Classes Must Use XCTest Framework with Proper Structure

issues.title: Incorrect tearDown order in StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests
issues.description: The tearDown method calls super.tearDown() before cleaning up test dependencies. In XCTest, super.tearDown() should be called after cleaning up resources to ensure proper cleanup order. Calling super.tearDown() first can cause issues when the parent class attempts to access or clean up resources that are about to be deallocated. The DependencyHelperMock().reset() and collectionView/diffableDataSource cleanup should happen before calling the parent's tearDown to prevent potential crashes or state inconsistencies between tests.

issues.title: Test state cleanup after super.tearDown in RatingPromptManagerTests
issues.description: The tearDown method calls super.tearDown() before cleaning up test-specific state (prefs, subject, userDefaults, etc.). This is problematic because XCTest's tearDown should clean up test-specific resources before calling super.tearDown(). By calling super.tearDown() first, any state or resources that should be cleaned up might leak into subsequent tests or cause undefined behavior. Specifically, calling prefs.clearAll() and subject.reset() after super.tearDown() violates the expected tearDown lifecycle and can lead to test isolation issues where one test's state affects another.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
override func tearDown() async throws {
        try await super.tearDown()
        prefs.clearAll()
        subject.reset()
        prefs = nil
        logger = nil
        urlOpenerSpy = nil
        userDefaults = nil
        crashTracker = nil
        subject = nil
    }

issues.title: Missing @MainActor annotation in EditBookmarkViewModelTests
issues.description: The EditBookmarkViewModelTests class is missing the @MainActor annotation that was added in the PR for Swift 6 concurrency compliance. This test class uses UI components (UITableView) and interacts with MainActor-isolated types. Without the @MainActor annotation, the tests may experience data races or undefined behavior when accessing MainActor-isolated properties, particularly since the setUp and tearDown methods are now async and the test methods interact with UI components. This violates Swift 6 concurrency requirements and can lead to runtime crashes or unpredictable test behavior.

issues.title: UI-related test lifecycle method not annotated with @MainActor
issues.description: This test creates/configures a UIViewController in setUp, which is UI work. Rule 9 requires UI-related code to be annotated with @MainActor (either on the class or the method). The modified setUp() signature is not annotated and the class is not marked @MainActor in the diff.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Mock class not marked final
issues.description: Per Rule 12, classes that are not intended for subclassing should be marked `final`. This mock type appears to be a concrete test helper and is modified in this PR, but remains non-final.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31130 - Refactor FXIOS-14344 [Swift 6 migration] Fixing warnings in unit tests

structured_output.summary:
This is a test-only Swift 6 migration. It converts many XCTestCase `setUp`/`tearDown` overrides to `async throws` with `try await super.setUp()`/`tearDown()`, adds or removes `@MainActor` on several test classes, and tweaks a few mocks (`final`, `@unchecked Sendable`, and a `@MainActor @Sendable @escaping` closure signature that matches the `TabQueue` protocol). The bulk of the mechanical migration is consistent and correct.

Two changes are risky. In `NotificationManagerTests`, the XCTest assertions were replaced with Swift `assert()` calls. That makes the test unable to report failures properly. In `EditBookmarkViewModelTests`, the class-level `@MainActor` was removed even though the test calls `@MainActor`-isolated members of `EditBookmarkViewModel`. I could not build on Linux, so the second one needs a compiler check, but the isolation mismatch is clear from the source.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The NotificationManager test now uses `assert()`, which is stripped in release builds and traps the whole test process in debug instead of recording an XCTest failure, so the test can no longer report a real failure. The EditBookmarkViewModelTests class lost its `@MainActor` while its tests call `@MainActor` methods from synchronous nonisolated code, which should produce a concurrency diagnostic or error. Both should be fixed before merge. The rest of the migration is sound.

architecture.overview:
The affected code is the XCTest layer under firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests. Each test class inherits XCTestCase lifecycle hooks, and many of them bootstrap shared DependencyHelperMock state and use mocks such as MockUserNotificationCenter. Nothing in the production app changes. The PR moves the lifecycle overrides to Swift concurrency-aware signatures (setUp/tearDown as async throws, with super called explicitly) and adjusts actor isolation on selected test classes and mocks.

The new behavior is concentrated in two spots. The NotificationManager test calls the production NotificationManager, which forwards to the mock center; the mock invokes its completion synchronously, so the assertion closure runs during the test. The EditBookmarkViewModel test used to be isolated to the MainActor at class level. With that removed, its synchronous calls into the view model's MainActor-isolated methods no longer have an isolated caller.
steps: Start at the XCTest runner, which calls each class's setUp (now async throws) and then each test method. Lifecycle bodies bootstrap DependencyHelperMock or create mocks, and tearDown resets them.

In NotificationManagerTests.testRequestAuthorization, the test calls NotificationManager.requestAuthorization. That forwards to MockUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization, which invokes the completion handler synchronously. The PR's assert() calls inside the closure replace XCTAssert calls, which changes failure reporting.

EditBookmarkViewModelTests exercises EditBookmarkViewModel, whose selectFolder and didFinish are @MainActor. The class-level @MainActor on the test was removed, so synchronous test methods now call MainActor-isolated APIs from a nonisolated context.

Mock changes are type-level only: MockTabQueue.getQueuedTabs matches the TabQueue protocol's @MainActor @Sendable @escaping completion, MockURLAuthenticationChallengeSender becomes final, and MockUserNotificationCenter becomes @unchecked Sendable.

findings.title: XCTest assertions replaced with Swift assert(), so failures are not reported
findings.body:
The original test used `XCTAssertTrue`, which records a failure in the XCTest report. The PR replaces these with Swift's `assert()`. That causes two problems:

- In optimized builds, `assert()` is compiled out, so the test always passes.
- In Debug, a failed `assert()` traps the test process. That aborts the whole test run instead of marking one test as failed.

The mock invokes the completion handler synchronously, so the closure does run, which makes the regression easy to miss. The assertions also read `center?.requestAuthorizationWasCalled ?? false`, which hides a nil center as a failure with no useful message.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Helpers/NotificationManagerTests.swift" lines="26-29"}

::callout{type="warning"}
The other tests in this file still use `XCTAssertTrue`, so this is an inconsistent change as well as a behavior regression.

::
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Helpers/NotificationManagerTests.swift`, `testRequestAuthorization` (lines 26-29) uses Swift `assert()` inside the completion closure. Swift `assert` is stripped in release builds and traps the test process in debug instead of reporting an XCTest failure. Restore XCTest assertions so failures are recorded, for example `XCTAssertTrue(granted)` and `XCTAssertTrue(center.requestAuthorizationWasCalled)`. Better still, use an `XCTestExpectation` or the async `requestAuthorization()` overload so the assertions run after the callback is definitely called. Follow the assertion style used by the rest of this file.

findings.title: Class-level @MainActor removed while tests call MainActor-isolated view model methods
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Library/Bookmarks/EditBookmarkViewModelTests.swift`, the class-level `@MainActor` was removed from `EditBookmarkViewModelTests` (line 11). The tests call `@MainActor`-isolated members of `EditBookmarkViewModel`, such as `selectFolder` (around line 60 and 76 of the test, and line 82 of `EditBookmarkViewModel.swift`). Restore `@MainActor` on the class, the same way the sibling `EditBookmarkDataSourceTests` and `MainMenuViewControllerTests` are annotated in this PR, so that the synchronous test methods and the async `setUp`/`tearDown` run on the main actor. Then build the test target to confirm the warnings are gone.

findings.title: Inconsistent tearDown ordering in RatingPromptManagerTests
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Helpers/RatingPromptManagerTests.swift`, `tearDown` (lines 36-38) calls `try await super.tearDown()` before the cleanup. Move that call to the end of the method, after `subject = nil`, to match the convention used by the other converted test classes in this PR (for example `IntroViewControllerTests` and `HistoryPanelTests`). Behavior is unchanged; this is only for consistency.

findings.title: Mechanical setUp/tearDown migration and protocol-matching mock changes are correct
findings.body:
The bulk of this PR is a straightforward migration. Most classes switch to `override func setUp() async throws` with `try await super.setUp()`, and `tearDown` mirrors it. The `setUpWithError` override in `StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests` is correctly converted to `setUp`. Each `@MainActor` addition (`StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests`, `EditBookmarkDataSourceTests`, `MainMenuViewControllerTests`, and the other view-controller tests) is a reasonable isolation choice for UIKit tests.

The `MockTabQueue.getQueuedTabs` signature `@MainActor @Sendable @escaping` matches the protocol declaration in `firefox-ios/Storage/Queue.swift:10` and `SQLiteQueue.swift:24`, so the mock still conforms. `MockURLAuthenticationChallengeSender` is now `final`, and a search found no subclasses. None of the changed test files lose a required `super` call.
